comparison: Both evaluations strongly support the structural claims (C19-C28, C64). OpenEval emphasizes the high-resolution crystallographic data and validation, while peer reviewers praised the structural analysis as 'excellent' and a 'significant contribution to the field.' Strong agreement on structural findings.

Both evaluations support the picomolar affinity of the LysM1-LysM3 site (C3, C40, C43). OpenEval cites crystal structure and ITC data, while peer reviewers explicitly stated 'the LysM1–3 binding site has sufficient affinity to work as the authors suggest.' Strong agreement on high-affinity binding and functional significance.

Both evaluations support LysM2's independent chitin-binding activity (C4, C41, C42). OpenEval finds convergent evidence from ITC and functional assays, while peer reviewers accepted the micromolar binding affinity measurements without challenge. Agreement on binding data, though peer reviewers questioned functional interpretation addressed in other results.

Divergence on mutant binding studies (C29, C30). OpenEval finds ITC data in Figure 3 supportive, while peer reviewers requested clarification on data fitting and model interpretation, indicating uncertainty about the presentation and analysis of mutant binding results.

Partial overlap on functional assays (C31). OpenEval supports claims based on alkalinization data, while peer reviewers requested better presentation, statistical analysis, and questioned interpretation of the tomato protoplast assay results, indicating uncertainty about functional data quality and interpretation.

Divergence on mutant autoactivity (C32, C33). OpenEval accepts the documented alkalinization without chitin as a clear negative result, while peer reviewers questioned whether mutants showing pH shift are truly non-autoactive and requested statistical analysis, indicating uncertainty about the interpretation.

Divergence on chitin-free protein production and ITC analysis (C37-C39, C71). OpenEval supports the methodology and two-site binding model, while peer reviewers requested control ITC traces and noted discrepancies with previous work showing three binding events, indicating uncertainty about data quality and interpretation.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding LysM2 mechanism (C5, C47-C52). Both evaluations recognize these as speculative claims. OpenEval notes lack of direct experimental evidence for receptor interference, while peer reviewers raised 'major concern' about the sequestration model and requested stronger conclusions that LysM2 works via alternative mechanisms.

Divergence on the paradox analysis (C47-C49, C72-C73). OpenEval supports the quantitative analysis identifying that LysM2 affinity is insufficient for sequestration, while peer reviewers expressed this as a major concern requiring resolution, indicating uncertainty about the functional mechanism despite accepting the binding data.

Both evaluations support the structural comparison with AtCERK1 (C45, C55). OpenEval emphasizes the novelty of intrachain versus interchain dimerization, while peer reviewers accepted this as part of the excellent structural analysis. Strong agreement on comparative structural findings.

Divergence on bound oligomer identity and binding mode (C66-C69). OpenEval finds inferences reasonable based on structural data, while peer reviewers questioned whether the oligomer is actually (GlcNAc)4 and suggested mass spectrometry confirmation, noting that longer chain binding remains speculative.

OpenEval evaluated background/contextual claims (C1, C6-C18, C44, C53-C54) as properly cited established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically focus on novel findings rather than background citations.

OpenEval evaluated methodological descriptions (C56-C63) as standard and sufficiently detailed. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as a discrete result, though peer reviewers did request specific methodological clarifications embedded in other results.
OpenEval evaluated the negative result about failed chitin removal from Pichia (C70) as appropriately documented. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this methodological detail.
